# Models

We develop a sequence of models of increasing complexity for the binary outcome
$y_i = \texttt{low3}_i \in \{0, 1\}$, which indicates whether respondent $i$
reports low institutional trust. All models share a common logistic-regression
backbone and the same set of socio-demographic covariates; later models extend
the baseline with hierarchical, monotonic, and smooth structure. Each model is
presented below in its own block, so that additional models can be slotted in
using the same template.

| Model | Specification | Type |
|:-----:|:--------------|:-----|
| **M1** | `low3 ~ age + econ5 + edu` | Non-hierarchical logistic regression |
| *M2* | *(to be documented)* | *Hierarchical (varying intercept)* |
| *...* | *(to be documented)* | *...* |

: Overview of the candidate models. {#tbl-models tbl-colwidths="[12,55,33]"}

## Baseline logistic regression {#sec-m1}

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Model 1 · Three-covariate logistic regression

The baseline model is a non-hierarchical Bernoulli logistic regression that
explains low trust through three categorical covariates: age group
(`age`), economic situation (`econ5`), and education level (`edu`). It serves
as the reference against which all later, more flexible models are compared.

**Model.** For respondent $i = 1, \dots, n$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
y_i &\sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_i), \\
\operatorname{logit}(p_i) &= \alpha + \mathbf{x}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{\beta},
\end{aligned}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_i$ is the vector of dummy-coded indicators for the levels of
`age`, `econ5`, and `edu` (reference levels absorbed into the intercept),
$\alpha$ is the intercept on the log-odds scale, and $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ the
vector of covariate coefficients.

**Priors (weakly informative).**
$$
\alpha \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 2^2), \qquad
\beta_j \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1^2).
$$

These priors are weakly informative on the log-odds scale: the $\beta_j$ keep
individual covariate effects within a plausible range (a shift of a few units in
log-odds), while the wider intercept prior allows for a broad baseline
prevalence of low trust.
:::

```{r}
#| label: priors-m1
#| eval: false
pr_base <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"),          # covariate effects
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "Intercept")   # baseline log-odds
)
```

Proper priors for every parameter, with a justification (weakly informative or

# Model code

```{r}
#| label: fit-models
#| eval: false
m1 <- brm(y ~ x, data = d, prior = priors_m1,
          chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, seed = 2026,
          file = file.path(fit_dir, "m1"))
m2 <- brm(y ~ x + (1 | group), data = d, prior = priors_m2,
          chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, seed = 2026,
          file = file.path(fit_dir, "m2"))
```

# Convergence diagnostics

R-hat, bulk/tail ESS, and divergences for all models. Summarise when there are
no problems, and describe any fixes.

```{r}
#| label: convergence
#| eval: false
summarise_draws(as_draws_df(m1), default_convergence_measures())
nuts_params(m1) |> filter(Parameter == "divergent__") |> summarise(sum(Value))
```
